record.paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
record.context_brief: Banach spaces with few approximable operators.
record.original_question: Find infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X for which the set app(X) of approximation-number profiles realized by approximable operators on X is strictly smaller than the full cone c_0^*(N) of nonincreasing null sequences. In other words, find Banach spaces that have few approximable operators, and ideally make app(X) as small as possible.

evidence.quote:
Problem 21. Find infinite-dimensional Banach spaces that have few approx￾imable operators.
Main goal: Make app(X) as small as possible.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. For a bounded linear operator $T \in \mathcal{L}(X)$, define the $n$-th approximation number
$$a_n(T) := \inf\{\|T - F\| : F \in \mathcal{L}(X),\ \operatorname{rank}(F) < n\}, \qquad n = 1,2,\dots .$$
The sequence $(a_n(T))_{n\ge 1}$ is nonincreasing, and $T$ is called approximable if it is the operator-norm limit of finite-rank operators on $X$, equivalently $a_n(T) \to 0$. Let $c_0^{*}(\mathbb{N})$ denote the cone of all nonincreasing sequences of nonnegative real numbers tending to $0$, and define
$$\operatorname{app}(X) := \{(a_n(T))_{n\ge 1} : T \in \mathcal{L}(X)\ \text{is approximable}\} \subseteq c_0^{*}(\mathbb{N}).$$
For a general infinite-dimensional Banach space one has $\operatorname{app}(X) = c_0^{*}(\mathbb{N})$. The problem is to find infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ for which the inclusion $\operatorname{app}(X) \subsetneq c_0^{*}(\mathbb{N})$ is strict, and, more ambitiously, to construct $X$ for which the cone $\operatorname{app}(X)$ is as small as possible (ideally close to a minimal nontrivial subcone of $c_0^{*}(\mathbb{N})$).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a survey on traces on operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces. No solution or substantive partial result identifying infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ with $\operatorname{app}(X)$ strictly smaller than $c_0^{*}(\mathbb{N})$ was found in the literature search. Related work on operator ideals and approximation properties exists, but does not resolve this question.

status_evidence.title: A New Approach to Operator Ideals on Hilbert Space and Their Traces
status_evidence.snippet: On infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces H, there exist no other ideals of approximable operators than certain specific forms. In the setting of Banach spaces, the situation becomes much more complicated.
status_evidence.claim: In the Banach space setting the structure of approximable-operator ideals is far less understood than in the Hilbert case, consistent with the question being open.

status_evidence.title: Approximation property - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Enflo's negative answer to the approximation problem implies that there exist compact operators between Banach spaces that cannot be approximated by finite rank operators.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of Banach spaces failing the approximation property is the only known mechanism limiting approximable operators; constructions making app(X) strictly smaller than c_0^*(N) remain unresolved.
